Subject: Re: Discovery — region pinning / data residency follow-ups

Thanks Vanessa — great call this morning. A quick recap and a few clarifying questions from our side: 

Summary of needs:
- Primary requirement: US data residency for customer chat transcripts and embeddings (stored and processed in us-west region).
- EU data residency for a subset of EMEA customers (we need region pinning by account).
- Cross-region failover: acceptable to fail over to a different region if primary is down, but must ensure no logs/backups are retained outside pinned region for >30 days.
- Logging controls: ability to disable or filter PII from audit logs is a must.

Questions:
1) Can Redwood guarantee that data for a pinned account will not be persisted outside the pinned region (including backups and asynchronous logs)?
2) What is your recommended approach for cross-region failover — automatic vs manual — and how does that affect data residency constraints?
3) For PII redaction in logs, do you offer built-in filters or would we need to handle redaction before sending?

If you can point us to any design docs or SOC2 artifacts, that would help our InfoSec review. Also copying Tara from our cloud security team who will own the detailed questions.

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Patel
Lead PM, Conversational AI
Acme Bank

Hi Samir — thanks for the clear recap and great discussion today. Short answers up front, then I'll attach the docs and propose next steps.

Quick answers:
- Region pinning: yes, we support account-level region pinning. Data (requests, responses, embeddings, and KV cache persistence) for a pinned account can be restricted to a single region. Backups for pinned accounts are also retained in-region by default.
- Cross-region failover: we support configurable failover policies. For strict residency customers we recommend a manual or policy-driven failover that requires Ops approval; automatic failover is available but will replicate state to the failover region (not recommended for strict residency).
- PII/logging: Redwood has an audit logging filter layer and built-in PII scrubbing options (configurable). We can also expose masked logs to your security team.

Attachments: I'm attaching a short design doc (redwood-region-pinning.pdf) and our SOC 2 summary (SOC2-summary.pdf).

Next steps I propose:
1) I'll share the two docs (attached).
2) Aditya (cc'd) can run a quick compatibility check on your sample traffic patterns — is it possible to share a 24-hour token profile (not PII) for sizing?
3) If InfoSec wants deeper artifacts, we can schedule a 30-min call with our Security lead and Solutions Engineer next week.

Proposed times: Wed 9/16 10:00-11:00 PT or Thu 9/17 14:00-15:00 PT. Which works for you and Tara?

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

Hi Tara / Samir — following up with the detailed notes from our infra/ops view. Answers below are written to be InfoSec-friendly; happy to jump on a call to walk through.

1) Backups/snapshots
- For pinned accounts we support disabling cross-region snapshot replication. Snapshots and backups are stored in-region (us-west) unless you opt into cross-region DR. We will provide a short policy to include in your security questionnaire stating: "Snapshots for pinned accounts will not be copied outside the pinned region unless explicitly enabled by customer Ops."

2) Cross-region failover
- Recommended pattern for strict-residency: manual failover via Operations or a policy with human approval. Automatic failover will replicate state to the failover region and is only recommended for availability-first use cases. We can implement an inline policy that prevents automatic failover for accounts flagged as residency-strict.

3) PII and logging controls
- We offer three options: server-side PII scrubbing (configurable regex rules), client-side pre-filtering (recommended for highest assurance), and redacted/partial logs for audit. Retention is configurable per-account; we can set default retention to 30 days and expose an API and console control for changes.

4) Artifacts and next steps
- Vanessa attached the SOC 2 summary and region pinning doc. We will share a sanitized log sample and a formal statement for your compliance team by EOD tomorrow.
- If you can share the token distribution sample, I'll run a sizing pass and provide recommended instance footprint + cost delta.

Proposed next step: 30-min InfoSec talk with our Security Lead (Marissa) + Solutions Engineer. I'll block Wed 9/16 10:00 PT as Vanessa suggested unless you prefer Thu.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
